description: Refers successful loading zone pilot update to Accessibility Advisory Committee.
New policy establishes process for accessible loading zones.
Eligible locations include schools, health facilities, community services.
Residential locations are excluded; zones are 6-10 meters long.
Signage restricts use to vehicles with accessible placards.

chips.text: Received as information
Cost of accessibility ramp is up to the applicant to cover.
Pilot project participants expressed high satisfaction with new accessible loading zones.
Improved access for people using mobility devices to buildings.

segments.title: Accessible Loading Zone Pilot Project Overview
segments.takeaway: Administration presented an update on the accessible loading zone pilot project, detailing its background, design, engagement, and proposed policy amendments for future installations.

segments.title: Committee Questions on Loading Zone Pilot
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked questions about ramp design, funding, enforcement, and the overall success of the accessible loading zone pilot project.

description: City reviews 2% target for accessible loading zones.
May add more accessible spots if current provision is insufficient.

chips.text: Councillor questions 2% accessible parking target, suggests 4-5% needed.
Public speaker supports loading zones, notes frustration with misuse.
Dedicated loading zones improve accessibility for people with disabilities.
Staff promises to revisit 2% accessible parking target if insufficient.

description: Increases on-street accessible parking in pay zones.
Sets design standards and location criteria for new spaces.
Prioritizes snow removal for accessible parking and ramps.
Committee seeks more feedback for a March review.

chips.text: Approved
Committee found the proposed 2% cap on Broadway insufficient.
Out-of-town visitors and regional users of city services.
Data on local accessible parking placard usage is not yet available.
Public speaker expressed strong support for accessible loading zones.
Accessible parking demand may be higher than the 2% proposed cap.
Staff committed to revisiting the 2% accessible parking cap.

segments.title: On-Street Accessible Parking Areas
segments.takeaway: Committee members discussed the current provision of accessible parking and loading zones, questioning the 2% target and considering data on placard usage.

segments.title: Accessible Map and Snow Clearing Concerns
segments.takeaway: Concerns were raised regarding the navigability of the accessible parking map for visually impaired individuals and the importance of snow clearing for accessible spots.

segments.title: Committee Feedback on Parking Areas
segments.takeaway: The committee passed a motion for members to provide additional feedback on the accessible parking areas by the next meeting for submission to administration.

segments.title: Work Plan Categories Review
segments.takeaway: The committee began reviewing its existing work plan categories, including deafblind services, transit, education, civic accessibility, and downtown transit.

segments.title: Access Transit Fleet and Demand Update
segments.takeaway: The Access Transit Manager provided an update on the transit fleet renewal plan, detailing new bus purchases and growth in client registrations and trips delivered.

segments.title: Motion to Retain Work Plan Categories
segments.takeaway: The committee passed a motion to retain its current work plan categories, deciding not to add or remove any subjects at this time.

segments.title: Work Plan Referrals Process
segments.takeaway: The chair explained the process for referring work plan items to the Standing Policy Committee, noting no items were being referred at this meeting.

segments.title: Subcommittee Memberships Discussion
segments.takeaway: The committee discussed the continuation of its Education Awareness and DeafBlind subcommittees, clarifying that subcommittees are not mandatory and can be formed as needed.

description: Future work plan will address Deafblind Services, transit, and accessibility.

chips.text: Approved
Work plan categories include Deafblind Services and Access Transit users.

description: Ad hoc subcommittees will form as needed.

chips.text: Approved
Members noted limited subcommittee activity and capacity issues last year.

description: Committee received an update on current city expenditures.
